title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: In agent design, the control flow is the order in which steps run and which step comes next. Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: In a workflow the program's code sets the steps; in an agent the model chooses them
In a workflow the model sets the steps; in an agent the program's code chooses them
A workflow never calls a language model, while an agent always calls one
A workflow calls the model once only, while an agent calls the model many times

items.stem: A makerspace assistant first asks the model to label each message as "manual question" or "booking request". Python code then runs a fixed manual-search path for the first label and a fixed booking path for the second. Who owns the control flow, and what is this?

options.text: The model owns it, so this is an agent, because the model made a decision
The model owns it, so this is an agent, because it calls the model
The code owns it, so this is a workflow; the model only supplies a label
The code owns it, so this is a workflow, because it uses only one model call

items.stem: A student has already chosen a machine, a date and a time, and confirmed. The assistant must check that the slot is free, write the booking, and send a confirmation email, always in that order. What is the best design for this part?

options.text: An agent, so the model can decide for itself whether to write the booking
An agent, so the model can invent a better order of steps each time
A fixed workflow, because the steps and their order are known in advance
A fixed workflow, because a workflow never needs to call any tools

items.stem: In one or two sentences: give one reason why a fixed workflow suits your team's small model budget better than an agent for a task whose steps are known in advance.

Every model call costs $0.01. A fixed workflow always makes 2 model calls per request. An agent makes 5 model calls per request on average. Your budget is $30. How many more requests can the budget cover with the workflow than with the agent?

A student asks the assistant, "My cut keeps burning at the edges; what should I change?" Nobody can say in advance which manual pages, settings checks or follow-up questions will be needed. In one or two sentences: is an agent or a fixed workflow the better fit for this request, and why?
